# Load/Store Unit (LSU) Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The LSU is the core’s memory-side functional unit for load, store, and atomic memory operations. It accepts memory instructions from the issue stage, computes their effective addresses, performs address translation when enabled, checks alignment and access permissions, interacts with the data memory system, and returns completion and exception responses to the scoreboard.

The LSU shall:

- Support byte, halfword, word, and doubleword loads and stores.
- Support word and doubleword atomic memory operations.
- Support integer and floating-point loads/stores.
- Preserve each operation’s transaction identifier from acceptance through completion.
- Report completion for loads and stores separately.
- Never make a speculative store visible to memory.
- Never return stale data to a load that aliases an older, uncommitted store.

## 2. Request Acceptance

The LSU shall accept memory-class instructions from the issue stage. Each request shall contain:

- The operation type (load, store, or AMO).
- The effective address operands.
- The data to be stored, for stores and AMOs.
- The access size and function.
- The transaction identifier.

The LSU shall advertise whether it is able to accept a new request. A request shall be accepted only when the LSU has sufficient storage/queue capacity. Accepted requests shall remain pending until they are processed or flushed.

The LSU shall ignore requests that are not memory operations; such requests shall have no effect on its state or outputs.

## 3. Address Calculation

For every accepted load, store, or AMO, the LSU shall compute a 64-bit effective byte address by adding the instruction’s immediate offset to the base operand. The addition shall be performed as signed two’s-complement arithmetic.

The LSU shall generate the appropriate byte-enable pattern based on the requested access size and the low-order bits of the effective address. The memory system shall observe the byte enables corresponding to the accessed byte lanes.

The LSU shall use little-endian byte ordering.

## 4. Load Operations

Loads may be issued to the memory system as soon as they are accepted and no ordering hazard prevents them. Loads shall not need to wait for a commit indication.

A load completion shall include:

- The same transaction identifier as the original request.
- The loaded data, when the load is successful.
- An exception indication when the load fails.

Loads may be outstanding concurrently. When multiple loads target the same address, their completions shall be returned in issue order.

A load shall not be allowed to read data that an older uncommitted store will modify. If such an address alias is detected, the load shall stall until the hazard is cleared. A load that is stalled for this reason shall not be issued to memory until it is safe to do so.

## 5. Store Operations

Stores are not allowed to modify memory while they are still speculative.

A store shall be held in the speculative store path until the core provides the commit indication for that store. The LSU shall provide commit flow control: it shall signal whether it can accept a commit request, and a commit request that is not accepted shall remain pending until the LSU can accept it.

Once a store is committed, the LSU shall move it to the non-speculative store path and eventually make it visible to the memory system. Committed stores shall not be discarded by a flush.

The LSU shall report store completion using the store transaction identifier. The completion shall be produced after the store is no longer speculative. For an ordinary store, the result data field is not meaningful; for AMOs, the read value is returned instead.

Store operations shall be kept in order with respect to other stores.

## 6. Atomic Memory Operations

Atomic memory operations shall be held until the core indicates that the AMO is no longer speculative. A speculative AMO shall not be sent to memory.

Once the commit/qualification indication is received, the LSU shall perform the AMO as a single atomic read-modify-write operation at the computed effective address. The value read from memory shall be returned as the result of the AMO.

Supported atomic operations shall include:

- Swap.
- Add.
- And.
- Or.
- Xor.
- Maximum and minimum, signed and unsigned.
- Load-reserved.
- Store-conditional.

For store-conditional, the result shall be the success/failure indication provided by the memory system.

An AMO shall obey the same alignment rules as a word or doubleword access. If an exception is detected before the AMO is performed, the AMO shall not be sent to memory and the exception shall be reported instead.

## 7. Memory Ordering and Hazards

The LSU shall enforce the following memory-ordering behavior:

- Committed stores shall become visible to memory in a deterministic order.
- A load shall not bypass an older store to the same address.
- A load may proceed past older stores to unrelated addresses.
- Stores to the same address shall remain in program order.
- Atomic operations shall not be performed speculatively.

The LSU shall provide a status output indicating when no store remains pending internally. This status shall be accurate for determining whether all accepted stores have drained from the LSU.

## 8. Exception Behavior

The LSU shall detect and report exceptions for memory operations. When an exception is reported, the memory operation shall not be performed.

### 8.1 Misaligned Address Exceptions

The LSU shall generate a misaligned-address exception when the effective address is not aligned to the access size:

- Doubleword accesses require 8-byte alignment.
- Word accesses require 4-byte alignment.
- Halfword accesses require 2-byte alignment.
- Byte accesses have no alignment requirement.

For loads, the exception shall be reported as a load-address-misaligned exception. For stores and AMOs, it shall be reported as a store/AMO-address-misaligned exception.

### 8.2 Non-Canonical Address Exceptions

When data address translation is enabled, the LSU shall use the SV39 virtual-address format. If bits 63:38 of the effective address are not all equal, the address is non-canonical, and the LSU shall report an access fault:

- Loads: load access fault.
- Stores and AMOs: store/AMO access fault.

### 8.3 Translation and Permission Faults

When address translation is enabled, translation or page-permission failures shall be reported as page faults:

- Loads: load page fault.
- Stores and AMOs: store/AMO page fault.

An operation that would fault must not be presented to the data memory system.

## 9. Address Translation and Memory Protection

The LSU shall support virtual-to-physical address translation for load, store, and atomic operations.

Translation shall be performed only when the relevant enable conditions indicate that virtual memory is active. When data translation is disabled, the effective address shall be treated as the physical address.

### 9.1 Translation Resources

The LSU shall use a translation cache to avoid walking the page table for every access. Translation lookups shall be qualified by the supplied address-space identifier.

The LSU shall accept a root page-table physical page number from the supervisor address-translation CSR and use it as the starting point for page-table walks.

The LSU shall also accept an instruction-fetch address-translation request interface. It shall service instruction-fetch translation independently from load/store translation, and shall return the translated address or an exception to the requester.

### 9.2 Page-Table Walks

On a translation cache miss, the LSU shall perform a page-table walk. Walk requests shall be given priority over load/store memory accesses when the memory system is contended.

A page-table walk that encounters an invalid or non-mapped entry shall produce the appropriate page-fault exception.

### 9.3 Permission Checking

The LSU shall enforce RISC-V page permission rules:

- Loads require the page to be readable.
- Stores and AMOs require the page to be writable.
- If the execute-only-read (MXR) mode is active, loads may also access pages that are executable but not readable.
- The SUM setting shall control whether supervisor-mode accesses are allowed to user pages.

The LSU shall use the privilege level associated with the load/store operation when checking permission for data accesses. Instruction-fetch translation shall use the appropriate instruction-fetch privilege information.

### 9.4 Translation Cache Maintenance

The LSU shall invalidate cached translations when a translation-cache flush request is received. After the flush, subsequent accesses shall not use stale translations.

## 10. Flush and Reset

On reset, the LSU shall:

- Discard all queued requests.
- Clear all speculative state.
- Have no pending stores.
- Not assert any completion or exception output.

On a flush:

- All speculative loads, stores, and AMOs shall be cancelled.
- No completion shall be reported for a flushed operation.
- Queued requests that have not been accepted by a load/store unit shall be discarded.
- Already committed stores shall remain in the non-speculative store path and continue to be written to memory.

A flush shall not by itself invalidate cached translations. Translation-cache invalidation is controlled separately.

## 11. Status and Performance Outputs

The LSU shall provide:

- A flow-control indication for accepting new requests.
- A commit flow-control indication for accepting store commits.
- A status indicating that no store is pending anywhere in the LSU.
- A data-translation-cache miss indication for performance counting.
- An instruction-translation-cache miss indication for performance counting.

These status outputs shall reflect the current state of the LSU and shall be suitable for use by the core’s control and performance-monitoring logic.

## 12. Completion Response Requirements

All load and store completion responses shall:

- Be asserted only when the LSU has produced a valid result or exception for a real, non-flushed operation.
- Carry the transaction identifier from the original request, unchanged.
- Carry the correct result data, or a valid exception, but not both.
- Not be asserted spuriously after reset or flush.

The LSU shall not drop a completed load/store response once it has been generated internally. Responses may be pipelined before leaving the LSU, but the transaction identifier and exception/data must remain associated with the correct operation.

# Memory Management Unit (MMU) Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Scope
The Memory Management Unit (MMU) translates virtual addresses to physical addresses for instruction fetches and for load/store operations. It contains separate instruction and data translation lookaside buffers and a hardware page-table walker. The unit supports the RISC-V SV39 address-translation scheme.

## 2. Translation Enable Modes
Instruction translation and load/store translation are controlled independently. When either mode is disabled, the MMU is transparent for that side.

- When instruction translation is disabled, every requested instruction-fetch address shall pass through unchanged, the corresponding fetch shall be reported as valid whenever the request is active, and the MMU shall not raise any instruction translation exception.
- When load/store translation is disabled, every requested load/store address shall pass through unchanged, the corresponding response shall indicate completion, and the MMU shall not raise any load/store translation exception.

## 3. SV39 Address Translation
When translation is enabled, the MMU shall translate addresses according to the RISC-V SV39 scheme and shall support 4 KiB, 2 MiB, and 1 GiB pages. The translated physical address shall be constructed by combining the page-frame information from the matching translation entry with the appropriate low-order bits of the virtual address.

## 4. Translation Lookaside Buffers
The MMU shall maintain two fully associative translation lookaside buffers: one for instruction fetches and one for data accesses. The number of entries in each buffer and the address-space-identifier width are configurable.

TLB entries shall be associated with an address-space identifier. Lookup shall consider only entries matching the current address space, unless an entry is marked global. A dedicated TLB-flush input shall invalidate all entries in both buffers.

## 5. Instruction-Fetch Translation Behavior
When instruction translation is enabled:

- The MMU shall check that the virtual address is canonical for SV39. If the address is not canonical, the MMU shall report an instruction access fault unless an instruction page fault takes precedence.
- On an instruction-TLB hit with sufficient execution privilege, the MMU shall present the translated physical address and mark the fetch as valid.
- Execution privilege shall be enforced as follows: a user page shall be executable only when the current privilege level is user; a supervisor page shall not be executable when the current privilege level is user; and a user page shall not be executable when the current privilege level is supervisor. Any violation shall be reported as an instruction page fault.
- On an instruction-TLB miss, the MMU shall perform a hardware page-table walk. If the walk succeeds, the instruction TLB shall be updated and the fetch may complete. If the walk fails, the MMU shall report an instruction page fault.
- The MMU shall not present a valid translated fetch while the translation has not yet been resolved.

When instruction translation is disabled, the MMU shall apply the transparent pass-through behavior described in Section 2.

## 6. Load/Store Translation Behavior
The data-translation interface is request/response.

For each active data-translation request, the MMU shall indicate whether the address hits in the data TLB when load/store translation is enabled. When load/store translation is disabled, this indication shall report that the address translation is complete without requiring a TLB lookup.

For each accepted data-translation request, the MMU shall produce a response that contains either:

- the translated physical address, or
- a translation-related exception.

If the request carries an externally supplied misalignment exception, that misalignment exception shall take precedence over any address-translation result in the response.

When load/store translation is enabled and no misalignment exception is present:

- On a data-TLB hit, the MMU shall evaluate data-access permissions.
  - A load requires read permission as determined by the current privilege level, the load/store privilege level, and the configured access-control settings.
  - A store requires write permission, a set dirty bit in the page table entry, and the same privilege checks as a load.
  - A permission failure for a load shall be reported as a load page fault; a permission failure for a store shall be reported as a store page fault.
- On a data-TLB miss, the MMU shall perform a hardware page-table walk. If the walk fails, the MMU shall report a load page fault or store page fault according to the request type.

When load/store translation is disabled, the response physical address shall equal the request virtual address and the MMU shall not generate any translation exception.

## 7. Page-Table Walks
On a TLB miss while translation is enabled, the MMU shall walk the page-table hierarchy starting from the root page-table physical page number supplied by the supervisor. The MMU shall issue memory requests through its dedicated page-table-walk memory port and consume the corresponding responses to obtain page-table entries. A successful walk shall update the appropriate TLB. An unsuccessful walk shall cause the MMU to produce the appropriate page-fault exception for the request that missed.

## 8. TLB Miss Performance Indicators
When instruction translation is enabled and a requested instruction address does not hit in the instruction TLB, the MMU shall assert the instruction-TLB miss indicator. When load/store translation is enabled and a requested data address does not hit in the data TLB, the MMU shall assert the data-TLB miss indicator.

## 9. Reset and Flush
On reset, the MMU shall enter a state with no pending translations, no pending responses, and no valid TLB entries. A global flush input shall discard any in-flight page-table walk and any buffered translation state so that no stale translation response is delivered.
